DECLARED LIMITATION: arena absolute WR is not live WR. Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: "measured ghost arrival = 25.5 control trades/day" alongside arms carried at stage [running/confirm] with a planned confirm n of 600.
findings.problem: The live tier holds 21 events total across a 60.7-day span, and the running arms report live_n=3 (control), live_n=1 (entry-8pct), live_n=2 (sl-5pct). An arrival rate of 25.5 control trades per day cannot be reconciled with those live counts, so the 25.5 figure is either a backfill-derived rate being presented as "measured" or it is measuring something other than scored control trades. Every schedule claim that depends on reaching n=600 inherits that error.

findings.claim: screen_dWR=0.0pp for entry-8pct and vol-4x, reported next to screen_wr=51.417 and 50.932 versus control screen_wr=49.772.
findings.problem: Both of those arms change a parameter that only subsets the detection stream (screen_n=494 and screen_n=858 versus control screen_n=1535). Their delta is being computed over trades both arms took, where the parameter cannot change any outcome, so 0.0pp is structurally guaranteed rather than an empirical finding. The arms' actual effect lives entirely in the events they declined, which the paired delta never scores. Reporting 0.0pp as a result makes an untestable arm look tested.

findings.claim: paired_population ok: "4785 events in the shared window; every arm has seen all of them", used to justify arm-vs-arm dWR comparison.
findings.problem: The still-open exclusions are unequal by arm — control 8, hold-12h 3, sl-5pct 10, tp-7pct 11, vol-4x 4 — and the scored counts differ correspondingly (control screen_n=1535 versus hold-12h screen_n=1540). Seeing the same events is not the same as scoring the same events. hold-12h shortens max_hold_h to 12, which mechanically resolves trades faster and leaves it the fewest exclusions, so the arm posting the headline screen_dWR=3.19pp is also the arm whose surviving-trade population is least censored. That is differential censoring, and the checkbox does not test for it.

findings.claim: backfill_cannot_promote ok: "0 surfaced arm(s); none promoted from a screen", presented as evidence the live-tape rule is enforced.
findings.problem: Events by tier are backfill 4764 versus live 21, so every screen_wr, screen_ev and screen_dWR in the arena — including sl-5pct at 5.22pp and hold-12h at 3.19pp — rests on backfill. The check passes because nothing has been surfaced yet, not because the rule was ever exercised against a candidate. A gate that has never had an input to reject has not been shown to work, and meanwhile the arms carrying backfill-only deltas are already labelled stage=confirm.

findings.claim: "MECHANISM CLASSES (one per running arm — diversity is enforced in code)".
findings.problem: The current arena contradicts it: control and entry-8pct are both class=entry_trigger, and placebo and vol-4x are both class=liquidity_filter. Either the enforcement excludes control and placebo without saying so, or it is not running. As stated, the constraint is described as an active code guarantee while the data shows two duplicated classes among the seven arms listed as running.

findings.claim: bonferroni_monotonic ok: "lifetime tests=6, pre-registered hypotheses=6; alpha=0.00833".
findings.problem: The recorded sl-entry-anchor kill judges its paired p=9.18e-41 against α=0.01250, a different correction than the 0.00833 the checkbox asserts is current. Three arms (dedup-24h, dedup-48h, sl-entry-anchor) were screened and retired, and the lifetime counter of 6 does not visibly account for them. A counter described as monotonic that coexists with a stricter historical alpha in the ledger has either been reset or is not counting every question asked.
